rows.what the ink shows: The second word retains two open c/e curves and a separate final i dot. The first begins with a tall loop, but its small following bodies are buried in the horizontal cancellation; Dans, Donc and a P-initial reading remain difficult to distinguish.

The low la and the following str-/t ascenders of structure remain visible below the inserted wording. The final word has a descending p-like loop, a dot and a tall medial stroke, but the cancellation and inserted text obscure enough letters that the full préhilbertienne is not secure.

The crossed sequence has an opening cup, a separate high dot, then a later looped ascending glyph and another dot near the end. Almost all connecting bodies lie in the cancellation, and these remnants do not securely establish une formule.
Between the parentheses the numeral has an upper rightward bow followed by a larger lower rightward bow. It has no flat top and left stem of a 5.

The upper phrase has the looped d, long f and dotted i strokes of définie, followed by a descending p and crossed t in positive. The nearby lower repetition is separately crossed and does not supply the upper word bodies.

A baseline u is followed by a detached low oblique stroke and a round glyph crossed by heavier ink; an additional u/w-shaped glyph sits above. The mark may include a canceled u,v pair with a replacement above, so the literal extent and replacement letter remain unresolved.

A shallow u-shaped trough survives after alors, followed by a distinct rounded loop sitting lower and to its right. The long line cancellation and a local diagonal overlap the loop, so u with a cancelled zero and u_0 cannot be distinguished confidently.

Two low word groups remain beneath the cancellation: the first has a short dark initial nub and a level trailing stroke; the second has a compact lower bend and another short horizontal. The individual s/t and d/a/n/s strokes are not sufficiently preserved to resolve the proposed words.

The baseline character has two short uprights joined by a shallow curved trough, supporting u. Immediately to its lower right, dense diagonal cancellation conceals further ink; whether a former index belongs to this character remains unresolved.

The second word begins with a small closed loop followed by low connected humps, compatible with aura, but its middle is crossed by the deletion. The first proposed word is reduced to a thick low dash with no separable o/n contours, so the whole reading remains uncertain.

The numeral has a short upright upper segment turning into a rounded rightward lower hook, matching the upright-and-hook body of the clearly written equation label 5 on this page. Its upper stroke is not the curled upper bowl visible in the earlier reference numeral; the detached top bar of the equation label is absent here.

Under the local diagonal overwriting, the cancelled capital retains an upright left stem, a lower horizontal foot and an upper arm fragment. These E-shaped remnants precede and overlap the rewritten E before the tensor sign; the following F is separate.
